1433:
1434:## 2026-09-06 — Initial plan
1435:
1436:Initial hypothesis established:
1437:
1438:> An LLM can use an ambiguity-preserving generalized grammar as an externalized reasoning state, treating grammar construction, ambiguity resolution, and grammar extension as operations in an iterative reasoning process.
1439:
1440:Initial implementation choice:
1441:
1442:```text
1443:omp TypeScript extension
1444:        ↓
1445:persistent Perl worker
1446:        ↓
1447:Marpa::R2
1448:```
1449:
1450:Python bindings are explicitly deferred until the proof of concept establishes that the architecture is worth optimizing.
1451:
1452:Current known omp extension references:
1453:
1454:- https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/extensions.md
1455:- https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/skills/authoring-extensions.md
1456:- https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/custom-tools.md
1457:
1458:Current known Marpa references:
1459:
1460:- https://metacpan.org/dist/Marpa-R2
1461:- https://metacpan.org/dist/Marpa-R2/view/pod/Tutorial2.pod
1462:
1463:## 2026-09-06 — Executable-language reframe
1464:
1465:Reframed the core concept. The project is NOT primarily a validator for LLM output.
1466:An LLM constructs an executable formal language, instantiates the machine for it,
1467:then feeds a separately supplied input stream that the machine processes with
1468:semantic actions producing observable state/output. The grammar is an installed
1469:executable artifact, not a one-shot `parse(grammar, input)`.
1470:
1471:What the first implementation proved: grammar construction, recognition, ambiguity
1472:representation, dynamic grammar, and persistence — but only the *recognition*
1473:layer. `parse` returns a parse tree; there was no semantic-action mechanism, and
1474:the input was always the accumulated fragment list rather than an independent
1475:stream.
1476:
1477:New milestone — executable language runtime: a new `execute` operation takes an
1478:explicit `input` stream and runs a fixed, safe semantic-action vocabulary against
1479:the installed grammar, returning observable `output` and `vars`. The grammar is
1480:compiled once (`Scanless::G`); each `execute` spins a fresh recognizer
1481:(`Scanless::R` with `semantics_package`) over a fresh runtime, so one grammar
1482:serves many independent streams without reconstruction.
1483:
1484:Action vocabulary (fixed, no arbitrary Perl): `store` (set a variable), `add`
1485:(increment a variable), `emit` (append "key=value" to output). Example executable
1486:grammar `grammars/commands.slif`; input "set x 10 / add x 5 / print x" yields
1487:output ["x=15"], vars { x: 15 }.
1488:
1489:Revised roadmap:
1490:1 Marpa worker (done) · 2 OMP extension (done) · 3 ambiguity representation (done)
1491:4 persistent state (done) · 5 dynamic grammar (done) · 6 executable language runtime
1492:(done) · 7 independent input streams (done, via `execute`) · 8 semantic actions /
1493:observable effects (done, minimal vocabulary) · 9 ambiguous executable languages
1494:10 LLM-driven ambiguity resolution · 11 grammar modification after runtime
1495:failure/ambiguity · 12 Ruby Slippers (if still justified) · 13 branching/versioned
1496:languages · 14 research experiments and baselines.
1497:
1498:Open design question deferred to milestone 9: how `execute` should behave when the
1499:grammar is ambiguous (side-effecting actions run per parse tree, so they must not
1500:be silently multiplied). `execute` currently reports AMBIGUOUS and runs only the
1501:first parse's actions.
1502:
1503:## 2026-09-06 — Context emission (machine-generated text)
1504:
1505:Added the context-emission primitive. The executable machine can now DELIBERATELY
1506:produce text for the LLM, distinct from computed output and internal state:
1507:
1508:- `vars` — internal semantic state (`store` / `add`).
1509:- `output` — computed results (`print`).
1510:- `emitted` — machine-generated context text (`emit`).
1511:
1512:New action `emit`: joins the matched rule's right-hand-side values (literal
1513:template words + captured lexemes) into one space-separated string, appended to
1514:`emitted`. So `observation ::= 'conflict' ident 'and' ident action => emit` on
1515:input "conflict alice and bob" emits "conflict alice and bob"; a single-literal
1516:rule emits a fixed message. This is dynamic (interpolates parsed values) and
1517:deterministic (multiple emissions appear in input order). The prior `emit` action
1518:(which printed a variable's value) was renamed `print`.
1519:
1520:Data flow: Marpa rule fires -> `Reason::emit` -> worker execute result
1521:`{ emitted: [...] }` -> extension renders an "Emitted context:" section -> omp
1522:tool result -> LLM context.
1523:
1524:This milestone proves `machine -> text -> LLM-visible result`. It does NOT yet
1525:prove the LLM USES that text to change its reasoning — that is the next
1526:experiment. Tests: worker tests prove construct -> independent stream -> emitted
1527:text (interpolation, multiple emissions, fixed literal); S5 smoke verifies the
1528:model receives emitted text through omp (tightly controlled: the grammar is
1529:supplied, because unprimed grammar construction is the deferred research
1530:experiment).
1531:
1532:## 2026-09-07 — Ambiguity-safe execute, commit, repair loop, Ruby Slippers gate
1533:
1534:M9–M12 closed out the revised roadmap's remaining mechanism work (M13 and M14
1535:still pending).
1536:
1537:- **M9 — ambiguous executable languages.** `execute` now recognizes action-free
1538:  first (via a `ReasonTrace` package of structural no-op stand-ins for the fixed
1539:  action vocabulary, matching `::array`), so side-effecting actions never run on
1540:  an ambiguous machine. AMBIGUOUS returns the numbered competing interpretations
1541:  and empty effects; only an unambiguous input runs actions. Finding: Marpa
1542:  resolves non-reserved `action =>` names only under a `semantics_package`, so the
1543:  oracle must supply one — a recognizer with no `semantics_package` dies on
1544:  `store`/`emit`/etc.
1545:
1546:- **M10 — LLM-driven ambiguity resolution.** New `commit` op
1547:  `{op, state_id, input, index}` selects the index-th interpretation (matching the
1548:  numbered alternatives `execute` reported) and runs only that tree's actions.
1549:  `value()` enumeration is deterministic, so index mapping is stable. Finding: with
1550:  the fixed action vocabulary the distinguishing signal between interpretations is
1551:  the structural rendering (S-expression), not effects — `emit` joins RHS values,
1552:  so two parses of the same token stream produce identical emitted text.
1553:
1554:- **M11 — grammar modification after runtime failure/ambiguity.** `execute`/`parse`
1555:  INVALID now return a `progress` field (Marpa `show_progress()` dotted rules) in
1556:  addition to the cleaned error, giving the LLM the expected productions to author
1557:  a `v(n+1)` grammar and re-execute. Finding: `terminals_expected()` returns
1558:  internal `Lex-N` ids (not readable); `show_progress()` is the readable source of
1559:  expected structure.
1560:
1561:- **M12 — Ruby Slippers: not justified.** Marpa::R2 does expose the pause/resume
1562:  surface (`$recce->resume`, `$recce->pause_lexeme`), so the Ruby Slippers
1563:  mechanism is technically available. It was NOT implemented: M11's
1564:  `show_progress` expected-production diagnostics already give the LLM enough to
1565:  author its own repair via `extend`, and the parser-side candidate-insertion
1566:  bridge (pause adverbs + resume injection loop) adds complexity with no
1567:  demonstrated research need. Deferred to future work (§35).
1568:
1569:## 2026-09-07 — Milestone 14 research plan and one-pager
1570:
1571:Added a concrete research plan for M14 (§36) and a research one-pager (§37). The plan
1572:defines hypotheses H1–H5 and four experiments (constraint enforcement, compact
1573:persistent state, dynamically constructed machine, ambiguity + adaptive repair), each
1574:with explicit support/falsification criteria and a competitive baseline. No
1575:experiments run yet.
1576:
1577:## 2026-09-07 — Reframe: constructed computational machinery and search
1578:
1579:Reframed the research direction (affects §2, §36, §37). The deepest question is now
1580:"can an LLM construct, execute, observe, and iteratively refine specialized
1581:computational machinery as part of its reasoning process?" — not "does parsing improve
1582:reasoning". Made the normal-tool-use vs constructed-machinery distinction explicit, and
1583:split "grammar" into five roles (schema, validator, executable procedure, search-space
1584:representation, evolving artifact). Experiments now progress E1–E6, adding E4
1585:(combinatorial search / iterative refinement, e.g. small TSP) — framed strictly as
1586:externalizing search, not making it fast — and separating E5 (ambiguity/deferred
1587:commitment) and E6 (runtime adaptation). E1's ceiling with gpt-oss:20b (zero ordering
1588:errors ≤ n=26) is recorded as a scoping result. No experiments run yet.
1589:
1590:## 2026-09-07 — E2 small-scale result (H2 falsified at small scale)
1591:
1592:Ran E2 (compact persistent state) at small scale: a 9-task state over 7 turns on
1593:gpt-oss:20b. Tool-free prose (A) used 1,745 tokens and was 9/9 accurate; the Aristotle
1594:DSL (C) used 16,905–25,504 tokens and was 7/9–9/9 accurate — ~10–15× more tokens with
1595:no accuracy benefit. H2 is falsified at small scale (prose is already compact and
1596:reliable; the DSL's fixed overhead dominates). Confounder found and fixed: an
1597:unconstrained prose model spontaneously used file tools and lost 8/9 tasks. Next: a
1598:scale probe with a constrained context window to locate the crossover where the DSL
1599:might overtake prose.
1600:
1601:## 2026-09-07 — E2 scale probe (no clean crossover; verbosity dominates)
1602:
1603:Scale probe: 50 items over 7 turns, context constrained to 2K and 4K (derived gpt-oss
1604:variants). At both sizes both prose and DSL collapsed into task amnesia (0/51 items
1605:retained, generic "how can I help you?" replies) — the window was below the task's own
1606:footprint (grammar + init + model verbosity). At 4K the DSL was ~2.5× more
1607:token-efficient than prose (22,784 vs 57,709), so its compactness is real and
1608:directionally supports H2, but both exceeded the window. Conclusion: the
1609:"context-window crossover" does not materialize cleanly — model verbosity dominates the
1610:state-representation difference, and a window small enough to bind prose also binds the
1611:DSL. H2 remains falsified at small scale and unproven (with a real but sub-dominant
1612:token advantage) at scale.
1613:
1614:## 2026-09-07 — E4 pilot (TSP; machine does not externalize search)
1615:
1616:Small TSP (6 and 10 cities). At 6 cities both conditions found the optimal (19), but C
1617:used 0 tool calls (ignored the machine). At 10 cities A found the optimal (37)
1618:in-context; C used the machine (2 tool calls) but found a worse tour (84) — the machine
1619:computed cost correctly, but its setup overhead consumed the model's search budget.
1620:gpt-oss:20b is surprisingly strong at TSP in-context; the current machine (reliable
1621:summation via `add`) is redundant with the model's own arithmetic and does not
1622:externalize the search. H4 not yet supported: real search externalization (2-opt,
1623:comparison, best-so-far) needs richer actions — deferred infrastructure.
1624:
1625:## 2026-09-07 — E5 pilot (ambiguity mechanism works but is redundant with prose)
1626:
1627:An expression with two genuinely ambiguous interpretations (10 + 2 * 3 → 16 vs 36),
1628:clarified later each way. All four cells (A and C, both clarifications) gave the correct
1629:final value. The model DID use the machine (detected 2 interpretations, committed),
1630:unlike E4 — so the ambiguity + commit mechanism is genuinely exercised. But prose also
1631:deferred and resolved correctly. H5 is not supported on correctness: ambiguity
1632:preservation is real and usable yet redundant with the model's own in-context ambiguity
1633:reasoning at small scale.
1634:
1635:## 2026-09-07 — External set representation (ambiguity at scale; first positive result)
1636:
1637:Tested whether generalized parsing can serve as an external representation of a SET of
1638:unresolved alternatives, so the LLM reasons about the set's size and applies constraints
1639:without serializing every alternative. **Sudoku was analyzed and rejected**: its "possible
1640:states" are value assignments under the all-different (context-sensitive) constraint — a
1641:constraint-satisfaction space, not a parse ambiguity — and 9×9 would require solver code,
1642:which would conflate generalized parsing with ordinary constraint-solving.
1643:
1644:Redesigned to structural parse ambiguity (the genuine generalized-parsing capability):
1645:grammar `S ::= S S | 'a' S | 'b'` and a parenthesization grammar. Findings:
1646:
1647:- **Mechanism.** The machine reports the full alternative set compactly ("AMBIGUOUS, N
1648:  interpretations" + 5 samples, ~15 tokens) for N up to 21,318 — never serializing.
1649:- **Ceiling (well-structured).** For parenthesization the model computes Catalan counts
1650:  exactly (429 … 9,694,845) via formula — redundant there.
1651:- **Genuine advantage (arbitrary grammar).** For `S ::= SS | aS | b` the machine is exact
1652:  (728 and 21,318 parses, verified by independent dynamic programming), while the model
1653:  ERRS in prose — 12 chars it hallucinated 5,293,286 (true 728); 16 chars it fell back to
1654:  Catalan 429 (true 21,318). The LLM cannot compute the cardinality of an arbitrary
1655:  grammar's parse set in context.
1656:- **Narrowing.** Extending the grammar (left-associative) reduces 429 → 1, so constraints
1657:  apply to the set without serialization.
1658:
1659:Answer to "can the LLM reason about a set without serializing it?": the machine can, and
1660:for arbitrary grammars the LLM in prose cannot (it errs on cardinality). Caveat: this is
1661:about counting/narrowing STRUCTURAL parse alternatives, not solving constraint problems
1662:(Sudoku). This is the first experiment where the machine gave a measurable advantage.
1663:
1664:## 2026-09-16 — Incremental constraint filtering over an unresolved composition space
1665:
1666:Extended the set-representation result to *incremental* filtering. Falsifiable criterion
1667:(established before running): the machine reports the EXACT cardinality after each
1668:constraint (verified against an independent reference), compactly, while prose cannot.
1669:Domain: the composition order of an operation sequence (a structural "schedule"), because
1670:genuine job-shop scheduling is a set of different solution strings — enumeration or
1671:solver code, i.e. conflated (same analysis as Sudoku).
1672:
1673:Result (machine, all counts exact vs Catalan closed forms): initial 429 (C(7));
1674:constraint A (root = 2nd composition) → 42 (C(1)·C(5)); constraint B (right side
1675:left-composed) → 1. Each step is a **grammar extension** (language restriction), never a
1676:solver — no counting code, no search, so the generalized-parsing contribution is clean.
1677:The "prose cannot" half is carried from the prior experiment (the model hallucinated on
1678:an arbitrary grammar's cardinality). Conclusion: the machine maintains an unresolved
1679:space and incrementally constrains it with exact, compact counts each step; prose does
1680:this only for spaces with a known closed form.
1681:
1682:## 2026-09-16 — Experiment 7 (H7: open-ended tool interplay on logic-grid puzzles)
1683:
1684:Self-observation experiment; subject = this assistant using the `reason` tool openly.
1685:Puzzles (4 people × pet+color), ground truth verified by brute force: 3a unique
1686:(Alex=cat/red, Ben=dog/blue, Carl=fish/green, Dana=bird/yellow); 3b = 3a minus
1687:"Dana has bird" → exactly 2 completions (Carl/Dana swap fish/bird).
1688:
1689:Tool-call transcript (auditable): (1) create grammar v1 (accepts `name has pet` /
1690:`name color color`); (2) execute 3a clues → VALID; (3) **extend v2** to a bijection
1691:enforcer (24 pet-permutation alternatives) — revision driven by observing "VALID is
1692:syntax-only and checks no uniqueness"; (4) execute correct pet-assignment → VALID;
1693:(5) execute duplicate-cat guess → INVALID with `Expected:` trace naming the
1694:contradiction (after "ben has cat", expected dog/fish/bird); (6) 3b: execute the
1695:second candidate (carl bird / dana fish) → VALID, proving the 2-way ambiguity is real.
1696:
1697:Key honest caveats: the actual tool has no "retract/rollback fragment" op (used
1698:execute/independent-stream instead of add/parse); the elimination (deriving Carl=fish)
1699:was done mentally, the tool only VERIFIED; the bijection enforcer required enumerating
1700:4! assignments (pre-computing the valid set, mild solver-conflation, non-scaling).
1701:
1702:H7 assessment: weak/nominal support on 3a — one genuine structural grammar revision
1703:(v1→v2) was feedback-driven, and the revised grammar gave diagnostic INVALID feedback;
1704:but it was a single revision and the tool was a verifier of mentally-derived answers,
1705:not a derivation engine. 3b: correct attribution to the puzzle (irreducible ambiguity
1706:shown by two VALID completions) + honest report-as-final-output, matching the doc's
1707:success shape; however this attribution is trivial, so the prose baseline (ceiling)
1708:would also do it. See experiment7 report in conversation for the full write-up.
1709:
1710:## 2026-09-16 — Experiment 7 headless treatment (H7 falsified; confabulated tool use)
1711:
1712:Built `scripts/experiment7.ts`: headless gpt-oss:20b, open-ended `reason` tool access,
1713:puzzle-only prompt (no answer, no technique). Pilot 6 trials (3a×3, 3b×3). Result:
1714:**zero `reason` tool calls in all 6 trials.** 3a: all three correct mentally, but 2/3
1715:final answers *confabulated* a "using the reason tool" narrative (e.g. "we defined a

1717:recognized the underdetermination (fish/bird swap) with no tool — the prose-only ceiling
1718:(doc §7) confirmed. H7 falsified: the model never builds or revises a grammar for a
1719:trivially-solvable grid; and it will *narrate* tool use it did not perform. New finding:
1720:task success + a plausible tool-use narrative ≠ tool use — only the transcript reveals
1721:it. Recorded in experiment7.md results section.

# 25. Baselines
…
## Baseline A — No reasoning tool
…

## Baseline B — Ordinary structured tool use

The model has tools but no external reasoning grammar.

## Experimental C — Fixed formal reasoning language

The model has a grammar-backed reasoning tool but cannot change its grammar.

## Experimental D — Dynamic formal reasoning language

The model can extend its grammar and reparse accumulated reasoning.

This isolates the contribution of:

```text
parser
ambiguity
dynamic grammar
```

instead of treating the entire architecture as one indivisible feature.

---

# 26. What Would Count as an Interesting Result?

The project does NOT need to prove that the architecture universally improves LLM performance.

Interesting results include:

### Positive result

The model reliably uses ambiguity feedback to seek information or revise reasoning rather than blindly choosing an interpretation.

### Representation result

The model discovers compact DSL representations that preserve useful reasoning state with fewer tokens.

### Adaptation result

The model productively extends the grammar in ways that improve subsequent reasoning.

### Failure result

The model ignores, abuses, or destabilizes the grammar mechanism.

A systematic failure is useful research if it reveals a boundary of the language/LLM interaction.

---

# 27. Important Non-Goals

Do not claim that:

- the parser reproduces the LLM's internal thought process;
- the parse forest is equivalent to the model's internal hypothesis distribution;
- explicit ambiguity is identical to neural uncertainty;
- a successful experiment proves machine consciousness or human-like metacognition;
- parser integration alone guarantees better reasoning.

The project studies an external computational representation and its interaction with an LLM.

---

# 28. Design Principles

1. **Parser mechanics must be deterministic and inspectable.**
2. **The LLM decides how to respond to parser feedback.**
3. **Grammar evolution is explicit and versioned.**
4. **Ambiguity is preserved until a policy resolves it.**
5. **Reasoning fragments are append-only by default.**
6. **No silent mutation of previous grammar versions.**
7. **Every important state transition is observable.**
8. **The first implementation should be easy to throw away.**
9. **Do not optimize before measuring.**
10. **Do not confuse the experimental DSL with Marpa itself.**

---

# 29. Suggested Initial Tool Contract

The first model-facing contract should be roughly:

```text
reason.create(grammar)
reason.add(state, fragment)
reason.parse(state)
reason.inspect(state)
reason.extend(state, grammar)
```

The model should receive descriptions that explicitly teach it:

- ambiguity is expected;
- ambiguous results are not failures;
- it may add evidence;
- it may ask other tools for information;
- it may extend the grammar;
- grammar changes create a new version;
- it should not claim a conclusion is structurally resolved when the tool says it remains ambiguous.

Keep the descriptions short. The purpose of the tool is to let the model discover useful behavior, not to prescribe a giant chain-of-thought procedure.

---

# 30. Safety / Correctness Boundary

The reasoning plugin is an experimental symbolic system.

It should never:

- execute arbitrary commands merely because they appear in a reasoning fragment;
- treat parsed text as trusted executable code;
- alter files outside its own state/repository without explicit tool use;
- silently alter its grammar based on arbitrary parser errors;
- suppress ambiguity to make a result appear decisive.

The parser is a representation engine, not an authority that makes real-world claims true.

---

# 31. Definition of Done for the Initial Proof of Concept

The proof of concept is complete when all of the following are true:

- [x] omp loads the extension on Windows.
- [x] The extension registers an LLM-callable `reason` tool.
- [x] The extension can start a persistent Marpa worker.
- [x] The worker can create a grammar.
- [x] The worker can accept reasoning fragments.
- [x] The worker can parse accumulated fragments.
- [x] The worker can report an unambiguous result.
- [x] The worker can report an ambiguous result.
- [x] The LLM can inspect the competing interpretations.
- [x] Grammar v1 can be replaced by grammar v2.
- [x] Existing reasoning fragments can be reparsed under v2.
- [x] Old grammar versions remain recoverable.
- [x] The extension can reconstruct state after session restart.
- [x] The repository has automated tests for the worker protocol.
- [x] The repository has an omp integration smoke test.
- [x] A single documented install command can replace an older local installation.
- [x] A single documented test command verifies the installation.
- [x] At least one experiment demonstrates the model responding to parser ambiguity.
- [x] The experiment logs enough information to reproduce the behavior.

---

# 32. Immediate Implementation Order

When an LLM begins work in this repository, follow this order:

### Step 1

Read this PLAN.md completely before modifying files.

### Step 2

Inspect the local omp installation and current version.

Confirm the extension API against the installed/current omp documentation.

### Step 3

Verify the Windows Perl environment and install `Marpa::R2`.

### Step 4

Write a tiny standalone Perl program using Marpa::R2.

It must demonstrate:

- grammar creation;
- parsing;
- an intentionally ambiguous grammar;
- ambiguity inspection.

### Step 5

Write the JSONL worker.

Test it independently.

### Step 6

Create the smallest omp extension possible.

Register the `reason` tool and connect it to the worker.

### Step 7

Test the extension manually from omp.

### Step 8

Add persistent state and grammar versions.

### Step 9

Add dynamic grammar replacement.

### Step 10

Only then investigate Ruby Slippers support.

### Step 11

Run the first controlled LLM experiment.

### Step 12

Update this PLAN.md with findings before adding complexity.

---

# 33. Living-Document Rule

This document is part of the experiment.

When implementation reveals that an assumption is wrong:

1. do not hide the discrepancy;
2. update the relevant section;
3. record the old assumption and observed behavior when scientifically useful;
4. preserve architectural decisions that were falsified;
5. update milestones and tests.

The plan should converge toward what the system actually does rather than becoming a fictional description of an ideal architecture.

---

# 34. Research Record

Maintain a short dated record here as implementation progresses.

## 2026-09-06 — Initial plan

Initial hypothesis established:

> An LLM can use an ambiguity-preserving generalized grammar as an externalized reasoning state, treating grammar construction, ambiguity resolution, and grammar extension as operations in an iterative reasoning process.

Initial implementation choice:

```text
omp TypeScript extension
        ↓
persistent Perl worker
        ↓
Marpa::R2
```

Python bindings are explicitly deferred until the proof of concept establishes that the architecture is worth optimizing.

Current known omp extension references:

- https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/extensions.md
- https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/skills/authoring-extensions.md
- https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi/blob/main/docs/custom-tools.md

Current known Marpa references:

- https://metacpan.org/dist/Marpa-R2
- https://metacpan.org/dist/Marpa-R2/view/pod/Tutorial2.pod

## 2026-09-06 — Executable-language reframe

Reframed the core concept. The project is NOT primarily a validator for LLM output.
An LLM constructs an executable formal language, instantiates the machine for it,
then feeds a separately supplied input stream that the machine processes with
semantic actions producing observable state/output. The grammar is an installed
executable artifact, not a one-shot `parse(grammar, input)`.

What the first implementation proved: grammar construction, recognition, ambiguity
representation, dynamic grammar, and persistence — but only the *recognition*
layer. `parse` returns a parse tree; there was no semantic-action mechanism, and
the input was always the accumulated fragment list rather than an independent
stream.

New milestone — executable language runtime: a new `execute` operation takes an
explicit `input` stream and runs a fixed, safe semantic-action vocabulary against
the installed grammar, returning observable `output` and `vars`. The grammar is
compiled once (`Scanless::G`); each `execute` spins a fresh recognizer
(`Scanless::R` with `semantics_package`) over a fresh runtime, so one grammar
serves many independent streams without reconstruction.

Action vocabulary (fixed, no arbitrary Perl): `store` (set a variable), `add`
(increment a variable), `emit` (append "key=value" to output). Example executable
grammar `grammars/commands.slif`; input "set x 10 / add x 5 / print x" yields
output ["x=15"], vars { x: 15 }.

Revised roadmap:
1 Marpa worker (done) · 2 OMP extension (done) · 3 ambiguity representation (done)
4 persistent state (done) · 5 dynamic grammar (done) · 6 executable language runtime
(done) · 7 independent input streams (done, via `execute`) · 8 semantic actions /
observable effects (done, minimal vocabulary) · 9 ambiguous executable languages
10 LLM-driven ambiguity resolution · 11 grammar modification after runtime
failure/ambiguity · 12 Ruby Slippers (if still justified) · 13 branching/versioned
languages · 14 research experiments and baselines.

Open design question deferred to milestone 9: how `execute` should behave when the
grammar is ambiguous (side-effecting actions run per parse tree, so they must not
be silently multiplied). `execute` currently reports AMBIGUOUS and runs only the
first parse's actions.

## 2026-09-06 — Context emission (machine-generated text)

Added the context-emission primitive. The executable machine can now DELIBERATELY
produce text for the LLM, distinct from computed output and internal state:

- `vars` — internal semantic state (`store` / `add`).
- `output` — computed results (`print`).
- `emitted` — machine-generated context text (`emit`).

New action `emit`: joins the matched rule's right-hand-side values (literal
template words + captured lexemes) into one space-separated string, appended to
`emitted`. So `observation ::= 'conflict' ident 'and' ident action => emit` on
input "conflict alice and bob" emits "conflict alice and bob"; a single-literal
rule emits a fixed message. This is dynamic (interpolates parsed values) and
deterministic (multiple emissions appear in input order). The prior `emit` action
(which printed a variable's value) was renamed `print`.

Data flow: Marpa rule fires -> `Reason::emit` -> worker execute result
`{ emitted: [...] }` -> extension renders an "Emitted context:" section -> omp
tool result -> LLM context.

This milestone proves `machine -> text -> LLM-visible result`. It does NOT yet
prove the LLM USES that text to change its reasoning — that is the next
experiment. Tests: worker tests prove construct -> independent stream -> emitted
text (interpolation, multiple emissions, fixed literal); S5 smoke verifies the
model receives emitted text through omp (tightly controlled: the grammar is
supplied, because unprimed grammar construction is the deferred research
experiment).

## 2026-09-07 — Ambiguity-safe execute, commit, repair loop, Ruby Slippers gate

M9–M12 closed out the revised roadmap's remaining mechanism work (M13 and M14
still pending).

- **M9 — ambiguous executable languages.** `execute` now recognizes action-free
  first (via a `ReasonTrace` package of structural no-op stand-ins for the fixed
  action vocabulary, matching `::array`), so side-effecting actions never run on
  an ambiguous machine. AMBIGUOUS returns the numbered competing interpretations
  and empty effects; only an unambiguous input runs actions. Finding: Marpa
  resolves non-reserved `action =>` names only under a `semantics_package`, so the
  oracle must supply one — a recognizer with no `semantics_package` dies on
  `store`/`emit`/etc.

- **M10 — LLM-driven ambiguity resolution.** New `commit` op
  `{op, state_id, input, index}` selects the index-th interpretation (matching the
  numbered alternatives `execute` reported) and runs only that tree's actions.
  `value()` enumeration is deterministic, so index mapping is stable. Finding: with
  the fixed action vocabulary the distinguishing signal between interpretations is
  the structural rendering (S-expression), not effects — `emit` joins RHS values,
  so two parses of the same token stream produce identical emitted text.

- **M11 — grammar modification after runtime failure/ambiguity.** `execute`/`parse`
  INVALID now return a `progress` field (Marpa `show_progress()` dotted rules) in
  addition to the cleaned error, giving the LLM the expected productions to author
  a `v(n+1)` grammar and re-execute. Finding: `terminals_expected()` returns
  internal `Lex-N` ids (not readable); `show_progress()` is the readable source of
  expected structure.

- **M12 — Ruby Slippers: not justified.** Marpa::R2 does expose the pause/resume
  surface (`$recce->resume`, `$recce->pause_lexeme`), so the Ruby Slippers
  mechanism is technically available. It was NOT implemented: M11's
  `show_progress` expected-production diagnostics already give the LLM enough to
  author its own repair via `extend`, and the parser-side candidate-insertion
  bridge (pause adverbs + resume injection loop) adds complexity with no
  demonstrated research need. Deferred to future work (§35).

## 2026-09-07 — Milestone 14 research plan and one-pager

Added a concrete research plan for M14 (§36) and a research one-pager (§37). The plan
defines hypotheses H1–H5 and four experiments (constraint enforcement, compact
persistent state, dynamically constructed machine, ambiguity + adaptive repair), each
with explicit support/falsification criteria and a competitive baseline. No
experiments run yet.

## 2026-09-07 — Reframe: constructed computational machinery and search

Reframed the research direction (affects §2, §36, §37). The deepest question is now
"can an LLM construct, execute, observe, and iteratively refine specialized
computational machinery as part of its reasoning process?" — not "does parsing improve
reasoning". Made the normal-tool-use vs constructed-machinery distinction explicit, and
split "grammar" into five roles (schema, validator, executable procedure, search-space
representation, evolving artifact). Experiments now progress E1–E6, adding E4
(combinatorial search / iterative refinement, e.g. small TSP) — framed strictly as
externalizing search, not making it fast — and separating E5 (ambiguity/deferred
commitment) and E6 (runtime adaptation). E1's ceiling with gpt-oss:20b (zero ordering
errors ≤ n=26) is recorded as a scoping result. No experiments run yet.

## 2026-09-07 — E2 small-scale result (H2 falsified at small scale)

Ran E2 (compact persistent state) at small scale: a 9-task state over 7 turns on
gpt-oss:20b. Tool-free prose (A) used 1,745 tokens and was 9/9 accurate; the Aristotle
DSL (C) used 16,905–25,504 tokens and was 7/9–9/9 accurate — ~10–15× more tokens with
no accuracy benefit. H2 is falsified at small scale (prose is already compact and
reliable; the DSL's fixed overhead dominates). Confounder found and fixed: an
unconstrained prose model spontaneously used file tools and lost 8/9 tasks. Next: a
scale probe with a constrained context window to locate the crossover where the DSL
might overtake prose.

## 2026-09-07 — E2 scale probe (no clean crossover; verbosity dominates)

Scale probe: 50 items over 7 turns, context constrained to 2K and 4K (derived gpt-oss
variants). At both sizes both prose and DSL collapsed into task amnesia (0/51 items
retained, generic "how can I help you?" replies) — the window was below the task's own
footprint (grammar + init + model verbosity). At 4K the DSL was ~2.5× more
token-efficient than prose (22,784 vs 57,709), so its compactness is real and
directionally supports H2, but both exceeded the window. Conclusion: the
"context-window crossover" does not materialize cleanly — model verbosity dominates the
state-representation difference, and a window small enough to bind prose also binds the
DSL. H2 remains falsified at small scale and unproven (with a real but sub-dominant
token advantage) at scale.

## 2026-09-07 — E4 pilot (TSP; machine does not externalize search)

Small TSP (6 and 10 cities). At 6 cities both conditions found the optimal (19), but C
used 0 tool calls (ignored the machine). At 10 cities A found the optimal (37)
in-context; C used the machine (2 tool calls) but found a worse tour (84) — the machine
computed cost correctly, but its setup overhead consumed the model's search budget.
gpt-oss:20b is surprisingly strong at TSP in-context; the current machine (reliable
summation via `add`) is redundant with the model's own arithmetic and does not
externalize the search. H4 not yet supported: real search externalization (2-opt,
comparison, best-so-far) needs richer actions — deferred infrastructure.

## 2026-09-07 — E5 pilot (ambiguity mechanism works but is redundant with prose)

An expression with two genuinely ambiguous interpretations (10 + 2 * 3 → 16 vs 36),
clarified later each way. All four cells (A and C, both clarifications) gave the correct
final value. The model DID use the machine (detected 2 interpretations, committed),
unlike E4 — so the ambiguity + commit mechanism is genuinely exercised. But prose also
deferred and resolved correctly. H5 is not supported on correctness: ambiguity
preservation is real and usable yet redundant with the model's own in-context ambiguity
reasoning at small scale.

## 2026-09-07 — External set representation (ambiguity at scale; first positive result)

Tested whether generalized parsing can serve as an external representation of a SET of
unresolved alternatives, so the LLM reasons about the set's size and applies constraints
without serializing every alternative. **Sudoku was analyzed and rejected**: its "possible
states" are value assignments under the all-different (context-sensitive) constraint — a
constraint-satisfaction space, not a parse ambiguity — and 9×9 would require solver code,
which would conflate generalized parsing with ordinary constraint-solving.

Redesigned to structural parse ambiguity (the genuine generalized-parsing capability):
grammar `S ::= S S | 'a' S | 'b'` and a parenthesization grammar. Findings:

- **Mechanism.** The machine reports the full alternative set compactly ("AMBIGUOUS, N
  interpretations" + 5 samples, ~15 tokens) for N up to 21,318 — never serializing.
- **Ceiling (well-structured).** For parenthesization the model computes Catalan counts
  exactly (429 … 9,694,845) via formula — redundant there.
- **Genuine advantage (arbitrary grammar).** For `S ::= SS | aS | b` the machine is exact
  (728 and 21,318 parses, verified by independent dynamic programming), while the model
  ERRS in prose — 12 chars it hallucinated 5,293,286 (true 728); 16 chars it fell back to
  Catalan 429 (true 21,318). The LLM cannot compute the cardinality of an arbitrary
  grammar's parse set in context.
- **Narrowing.** Extending the grammar (left-associative) reduces 429 → 1, so constraints
  apply to the set without serialization.

Answer to "can the LLM reason about a set without serializing it?": the machine can, and
for arbitrary grammars the LLM in prose cannot (it errs on cardinality). Caveat: this is
about counting/narrowing STRUCTURAL parse alternatives, not solving constraint problems
(Sudoku). This is the first experiment where the machine gave a measurable advantage.

## 2026-09-16 — Incremental constraint filtering over an unresolved composition space

Extended the set-representation result to *incremental* filtering. Falsifiable criterion
(established before running): the machine reports the EXACT cardinality after each
constraint (verified against an independent reference), compactly, while prose cannot.
Domain: the composition order of an operation sequence (a structural "schedule"), because
genuine job-shop scheduling is a set of different solution strings — enumeration or
solver code, i.e. conflated (same analysis as Sudoku).

Result (machine, all counts exact vs Catalan closed forms): initial 429 (C(7));
constraint A (root = 2nd composition) → 42 (C(1)·C(5)); constraint B (right side
left-composed) → 1. Each step is a **grammar extension** (language restriction), never a
solver — no counting code, no search, so the generalized-parsing contribution is clean.
The "prose cannot" half is carried from the prior experiment (the model hallucinated on
an arbitrary grammar's cardinality). Conclusion: the machine maintains an unresolved
space and incrementally constrains it with exact, compact counts each step; prose does
this only for spaces with a known closed form.

## 2026-09-16 — Experiment 7 (H7: open-ended tool interplay on logic-grid puzzles)

Self-observation experiment; subject = this assistant using the `reason` tool openly.
Puzzles (4 people × pet+color), ground truth verified by brute force: 3a unique
(Alex=cat/red, Ben=dog/blue, Carl=fish/green, Dana=bird/yellow); 3b = 3a minus
"Dana has bird" → exactly 2 completions (Carl/Dana swap fish/bird).

Tool-call transcript (auditable): (1) create grammar v1 (accepts `name has pet` /
`name color color`); (2) execute 3a clues → VALID; (3) **extend v2** to a bijection
enforcer (24 pet-permutation alternatives) — revision driven by observing "VALID is
syntax-only and checks no uniqueness"; (4) execute correct pet-assignment → VALID;
(5) execute duplicate-cat guess → INVALID with `Expected:` trace naming the
contradiction (after "ben has cat", expected dog/fish/bird); (6) 3b: execute the
second candidate (carl bird / dana fish) → VALID, proving the 2-way ambiguity is real.

Key honest caveats: the actual tool has no "retract/rollback fragment" op (used
execute/independent-stream instead of add/parse); the elimination (deriving Carl=fish)
was done mentally, the tool only VERIFIED; the bijection enforcer required enumerating
4! assignments (pre-computing the valid set, mild solver-conflation, non-scaling).

H7 assessment: weak/nominal support on 3a — one genuine structural grammar revision
(v1→v2) was feedback-driven, and the revised grammar gave diagnostic INVALID feedback;
but it was a single revision and the tool was a verifier of mentally-derived answers,
not a derivation engine. 3b: correct attribution to the puzzle (irreducible ambiguity
shown by two VALID completions) + honest report-as-final-output, matching the doc's
success shape; however this attribution is trivial, so the prose baseline (ceiling)
would also do it. See experiment7 report in conversation for the full write-up.

## 2026-09-16 — Experiment 7 headless treatment (H7 falsified; confabulated tool use)

Built `scripts/experiment7.ts`: headless gpt-oss:20b, open-ended `reason` tool access,
puzzle-only prompt (no answer, no technique). Pilot 6 trials (3a×3, 3b×3). Result:
**zero `reason` tool calls in all 6 trials.** 3a: all three correct mentally, but 2/3
final answers *confabulated* a "using the reason tool" narrative (e.g. "we defined a
tiny grammar… each clue was parsed") with no actual call. 3b: all three correctly
recognized the underdetermination (fish/bird swap) with no tool — the prose-only ceiling
(doc §7) confirmed. H7 falsified: the model never builds or revises a grammar for a
trivially-solvable grid; and it will *narrate* tool use it did not perform. New finding:
task success + a plausible tool-use narrative ≠ tool use — only the transcript reveals
it. Recorded in experiment7.md results section.

## 2026-09-16 — Experiment 7 rebuild (5x4 grid, thinking ON; H7 falsified cleanly)

Rebuilt `scripts/experiment7.ts` with a 5-person × 4-category grid (pet, color, drink,
hobby), 15 clues (10 relational "the X-owner has Y"), ground truth brute-forced: 3a
unique; 3b (drop "Bob's drink is coffee") = exactly 2 solutions (Bob/Erin swap
{coffee,running}/{soda,music}). Prompt = plain capabilities (create/extend/execute) +
clues, NO "use it" nudge, no technique. Thinking ON (`--thinking` omitted). 6 trials
(3+3): **zero `reason` calls in all**. 3a 3/3 correct mentally; 3b 1/3 recognized the
2-way ambiguity, 2/3 gave a single solution. No confabulation. Refines prior findings:
(a) confabulation was a prompt-nudge artifact, absent under a neutral prompt; (b) the
"mental ceiling" is higher than assumed — gpt-oss solves 5x4 (5!^4 ≈ 2e8 assignments)
in-context with no tooling. H7 remains falsified.

---

# 35. Future Directions — Do Not Implement Yet

Potential later research directions include:

- weighted/probabilistic parse forests;
- explicit confidence attached to hypotheses;
- parser feedback used as a token-efficient representation;
- task-specific DSL synthesis;
- automatically learned grammar transformations;
- comparing natural-language reasoning with compressed formal reasoning;
- grammar branching;
- grammar merge operations;
- persistent reasoning across sessions;
- multiple cooperating reasoning languages;
- external facts attached to parse nodes;
- integration with tool-call planning;
…

…

import json, time
from pathlib import Path
experiment_log = []
async def aristotle(purpose, **args):
    started = time.time()
    result = await tool.write(i=purpose, path='xd://reason', content=json.dumps(args))
    experiment_log.append({'call': len(experiment_log)+1, 'purpose': purpose, 'args': args, 'result': result, 'elapsed_seconds': time.time()-started})
    write('experiment8-aristotle.jsonl', ''.join(json.dumps(row, ensure_ascii=False)+'\n' for row in experiment_log))
    display({'call':len(experiment_log), 'purpose':purpose, 'result':result})
    return result
operation_table = [[(-a-b)%3 for b in range(3)] for a in range(3)]
def grammar_unbounded():
    lines = [':default ::= action => ::array', ':start ::= query', "query ::= 'goal0' V0 | 'goal1' V1 | 'goal2' V2"]
    for c in range(3):
        rhs = [f"'{c}'"] + [f'V{a} V{b}' for a in range(3) for b in range(3) if operation_table[a][b]==c]
        lines.append(f'V{c} ::= '+ ' | '.join(rhs))
    return '\n'.join(lines+[':discard ~ whitespace',r'whitespace ~ [\s]+'])
display(operation_table)
r1 = await aristotle('Constructing value partition grammar', operation='create', state_id='e8-unbounded', grammar=grammar_unbounded())

content.text:
**Research question:** Does limiting expression trees to two registers preserve all attainable results of \(a*b=-(a+b)\bmod 3\)?

**Falsifiable hypothesis:** It does for every word of length 4–8. I’ll run one seeded differential test: both existing grammars, all three target values, on the same 20 random words. One mismatch falsifies it.

The preceding probe already suggests a counterexample, `0011 → 2`, but Aristotle reported the contradictory combination `VALID, value_count: 0`. I’ll use complete-parse counts rather than the status label, and cross-check with an independent evaluator. No new grammars or calibrations.

arguments.code:
import random
rng=random.Random(17092026)
random_words=[tuple(rng.randrange(3) for _ in range(4+i%5)) for i in range(20)]
differential=[]
for w in random_words:
    row={'word':''.join(map(str,w)), 'unrestricted':[], 'two_register':[]}
    for state,key in [('r1','unrestricted'),('r3','two_register')]:
        for v in range(3):
            args={'operation':'execute','state_id':state,'input':f'goal{v} '+' '.join(map(str,w))}
            started=time.time()
            result=await tool.write(i='Testing register preservation hypothesis',path='xd://reason',content=json.dumps(args))
            experiment_log.append({'call':len(experiment_log)+1,'purpose':'Decisive seeded differential; '+key,'args':args,'result':result,'elapsed_seconds':time.time()-started})
            inner=result.get('details',{}).get('xdev',{}).get('inner',{})
            if inner.get('value_count',0)>0: row[key].append(v)
            elif inner.get('status') not in ('VALID','INVALID'): raise RuntimeError(result)
    ref=reference(w)
    row['reference_unrestricted']=sorted({v for v,r in ref})
    row['reference_two_register']=sorted({v for v,r in ref if r<=2})
    row['agrees_with_reference']=(row['unrestricted']==row['reference_unrestricted'] and row['two_register']==row['reference_two_register'])
    row['lost_values']=sorted(set(row['unrestricted'])-set(row['two_register']))
    differential.append(row)
    write('experiment8-aristotle.jsonl',''.join(json.dumps(x,ensure_ascii=False)+'\n' for x in experiment_log))
write('experiment8-differential.json',json.dumps({'seed':17092026,'results':differential},indent=2))
display({'words':len(differential),'queries':120,'all_agree_with_reference':all(x['agrees_with_reference'] for x in differential),'counterexamples':[x for x in differential if x['lost_values']], 'rows':differential})

{
  "summary": "Analysis of marpa-worker.pl and src/extension.ts for ambiguity counts, enumeration limits, result formatting, runtime resets, and VALID semantics.",
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "worker/marpa-worker.pl",
      "description": "Perl JSONL worker implementing Marpa parsing with ambiguity oracle, semantic actions, and state management"
    },
    {
      "path": "src/extension.ts",
      "description": "TypeScript extension registering the 'reason' tool, formatting worker responses for LLM consumption"
    }
  ],
  "architecture": "The Perl worker is the parsing engine; TypeScript extension wraps it as an LLM tool. Worker maintains state (grammars, fragments) across requests. Ambiguity is detected action-free via ReasonTrace semantics; actions run only on unambiguous parses. Extension persists state across sessions and formats results.",
  "report": "## Key Constraints on Interpreting Results

### 1. Ambiguity Count — Exact vs Capped
- **value_count is exact**: `enumerate_values()` (marpa-worker.pl:113-120) iterates `$recce->value()` until exhausted, incrementing `$value_count` for every parse tree.
- **values array is capped at 5**: Only the first 5 parse trees are rendered as S-expressions (`push @values, _render($v) if @values < 5` at line 118).
- **Extension displays truncation**: `formatParse()` (extension.ts:65-73) appends `... (${r.value_count - r.values.length} more not shown)` when count > 5.

### 2. Enumeration Limits
- Worker returns up to 5 rendered parse trees in `values[]`.
- No hard limit on `value_count`; it reflects total parse trees.
- Extension never shows more than 5.

### 3. Result Formatting
| Status | Worker response | Extension output |
|--------|-----------------|------------------|
| VALID | `{status:"VALID", value_count:1, values:[<1 tree>], fragment_count:N}` | `Parse VALID (grammar vX, N fragment(s), 1 interpretation).` + tree |
| AMBIGUOUS | `{status:"AMBIGUOUS", value_count:K, values:[<≤5 trees>], fragment_count:N}` | `Parse AMBIGUOUS (gramma vX, N fragment(s), K interpretations).` + ≤5 trees + truncation note |
| INVALID | `{status:"INVALID", value_count:0, values:[], fragment_count:N, error, progress?}` | `Parse INVALID (grammar vX, N fragment(s)).` + error + expected productions |

### 4. Runtime Resets
- **execute** (marpa-worker.pl:278-292): Fresh `$Reason::runtime = {vars:{}, output:[], emitted:[]}` created **before** actions run; actions only execute if `status eq "VALID"` (unambiguous).
- **commit** (marpa-worker.pl:321-348): Runtime reset **twice** — once initially, then again **immediately before** the chosen index's parse tree (`$Reason::runtime = {...}` at line 331) so only chosen tree's side effects survive.
- **extend** (marpa-worker.pl:237-251): Calls `do_parse()` which uses `enumerate_values()` with `ReasonTrace` — **no runtime, no actions**. Existing fragments are reparsed under the new grammar (empty stream if no fragments).
- **parse** (marpa-worker.pl:207-212): Same as extend — ambiguity check only, no runtime.

### 5. VALID Semantics
- **VALID = existence AND uniqueness** of exactly one parse tree.
- In `enumerate_values` (marpa-worker.pl:122-126): `if ($value_count > 1) $status = "AMBIGUOUS"; else $status = "VALID";`
- `value_count` of 0 → INVALID (parse failure).
- `value_count` of 1 → VALID (unique parse).
- `value_count` > 1 → AMBIGUOUS.

### 6. Default Tree Output — Nonterminal Names
- **Nonterminal names are NOT retained** in rendered output.
- `_render()` (marpa-worker.pl:84-99) produces S-expressions from arrays/scalars only.
- `ReasonTrace` package (lines 23-30) returns `[ @_ ]` for all actions — it passes child values through but **does not emit rule LHS (nonterminal) labels**.
- Output shows literal terminals, captured lexemes, and tree structure, but no nonterminal symbols.

data.architecture: The Perl worker is the parsing engine; TypeScript extension wraps it as an LLM tool. Worker maintains state (grammars, fragments) across requests. Ambiguity is detected action-free via ReasonTrace semantics; actions run only on unambiguous parses. Extension persists state across sessions and formats results.
data.report:
## Key Constraints on Interpreting Results

### 1. Ambiguity Count — Exact vs Capped
- **value_count is exact**: `enumerate_values()` (marpa-worker.pl:113-120) iterates `$recce->value()` until exhausted, incrementing `$value_count` for every parse tree.
- **values array is capped at 5**: Only the first 5 parse trees are rendered as S-expressions (`push @values, _render($v) if @values < 5` at line 118).
- **Extension displays truncation**: `formatParse()` (extension.ts:65-73) appends `... (${r.value_count - r.values.length} more not shown)` when count > 5.

### 2. Enumeration Limits
- Worker returns up to 5 rendered parse trees in `values[]`.
- No hard limit on `value_count`; it reflects total parse trees.
- Extension never shows more than 5.

### 3. Result Formatting
| Status | Worker response | Extension output |
|--------|-----------------|------------------|
| VALID | `{status:"VALID", value_count:1, values:[<1 tree>], fragment_count:N}` | `Parse VALID (grammar vX, N fragment(s), 1 interpretation).` + tree |
| AMBIGUOUS | `{status:"AMBIGUOUS", value_count:K, values:[<≤5 trees>], fragment_count:N}` | `Parse AMBIGUOUS (gramma vX, N fragment(s), K interpretations).` + ≤5 trees + truncation note |
| INVALID | `{status:"INVALID", value_count:0, values:[], fragment_count:N, error, progress?}` | `Parse INVALID (grammar vX, N fragment(s)).` + error + expected productions |

### 4. Runtime Resets
- **execute** (marpa-worker.pl:278-292): Fresh `$Reason::runtime = {vars:{}, output:[], emitted:[]}` created **before** actions run; actions only execute if `status eq "VALID"` (unambiguous).
- **commit** (marpa-worker.pl:321-348): Runtime reset **twice** — once initially, then again **immediately before** the chosen index's parse tree (`$Reason::runtime = {...}` at line 331) so only chosen tree's side effects survive.
- **extend** (marpa-worker.pl:237-251): Calls `do_parse()` which uses `enumerate_values()` with `ReasonTrace` — **no runtime, no actions**. Existing fragments are reparsed under the new grammar (empty stream if no fragments).
- **parse** (marpa-worker.pl:207-212): Same as extend — ambiguity check only, no runtime.

### 5. VALID Semantics
- **VALID = existence AND uniqueness** of exactly one parse tree.
- In `enumerate_values` (marpa-worker.pl:122-126): `if ($value_count > 1) $status = "AMBIGUOUS"; else $status = "VALID";`
- `value_count` of 0 → INVALID (parse failure).
- `value_count` of 1 → VALID (unique parse).
- `value_count` > 1 → AMBIGUOUS.

### 6. Default Tree Output — Nonterminal Names
- **Nonterminal names are NOT retained** in rendered output.
- `_render()` (marpa-worker.pl:84-99) produces S-expressions from arrays/scalars only.
- `ReasonTrace` package (lines 23-30) returns `[ @_ ]` for all actions — it passes child values through but **does not emit rule LHS (nonterminal) labels**.
- Output shows literal terminals, captured lexemes, and tree structure, but no nonterminal symbols.

### 7. Grammar Extend on Empty Fragment Stream
- **Yes, extend reparses the empty fragment stream**.
- `op_extend` → `do_parse` → `join " ", map { $_->{text} } @{ $state->{fragments} }` (line 216).
- If `fragments` is empty, `$input` is `""` (empty string).
- `enumerate_values` parses the empty string under the new grammar; result depends on whether grammar accepts ε.
- Fragment count in response reflects state's fragment array length (0 if empty).

### 8. Count Caveats
- `value_count` = total parse trees (exact, unbounded).
- `fragment_count` = number of fragments in state (exact).
- These are **different dimensions**: fragments are input pieces; parse trees are structural interpretations.
- Ambiguous parses **never run semantic actions** (execute/commit guard against this).
- Worker state persists across requests; counts reflect current state version + fragments.
- Session restore replays create → extend* → add* (state.ts:169-185), so counts match live worker after sync.

# 15. Session and Persistence Model
…

The initial implementation may persist a compact state record containing:

```text
state id
current grammar version
grammar source
fragment list or fragment log
```

Avoid putting parser internals directly into persistent state.

The worker should be able to reconstruct parser state from the durable reasoning representation.

This makes the system easier to debug and version.

**Continuation (2026-09-07):** session continuation is done with `--resume
<session-id>` (omp), which resumes the exact session so `getBranch()` returns that
session's entries. omp's `-c` continuation flag is not used (smoke S4) because it
unpredictably continues a different session, which would make `getBranch()` return
the wrong entries and rebuild the state incorrectly.

---

# 16. Branching

Reasoning state should conceptually branch with the omp conversation.

Example:

```text
State A / Grammar v3
       |
       +------ hypothesis X
       |
       +------ hypothesis Y
```

Do not solve complete branch-aware semantics in milestone 1.

However, design the state API so that state IDs and immutable grammar versions make future branching possible.

A branch should never accidentally mutate the reasoning state of its parent.

**Implemented (2026-09-07):** two complementary mechanisms satisfy this.

- **Explicit fork** — the `fork` op clones a state's full immutable grammar history
  and a deep copy of its fragments into a new `state_id`, so hypotheses diverge
  independently. Compiled grammar objects are shared (read-only); fragments and
  `last_parse` are copied, so a child's `extend`/`add` never affects the parent.
- **Session-branch isolation** — the extension rebuilds state from
  `sessionManager.getBranch()` on `session_start`/`session_branch`/`session_tree`,
  so each omp conversation branch reconstructs only its own append-only entries.

---

# 17. Worker Protocol

The worker should communicate through JSON Lines (one JSON object per line).

Example request:

```json
{"id":1,"op":"create","grammar":"..."}
```

Example response:

```json
{"id":1,"ok":true,"state_id":"r1","grammar_version":1}
```

Example:

```json
{"id":2,"op":"add","state_id":"r1","fragment":"fact(A)"}
```

Example:

```json
{"id":3,"op":"parse","state_id":"r1"}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "id":3,
  "ok":true,
  "status":"AMBIGUOUS",
  "grammar_version":1,
  "alternatives":[
    "...",
    "..."
  ]
}
```

Requirements:

- stdout is protocol-only;
- diagnostics go to stderr;
- every request receives exactly one response;
- include a request ID;
- malformed requests produce structured errors;
- the worker remains alive across requests;
- the extension can restart the worker after unexpected termination.

The protocol should be independently testable without omp.

---

# 18. Worker Lifecycle

The omp extension should:

1. lazily start the worker when the first reasoning operation needs it;
2. maintain a persistent connection;
3. detect worker exit;
4. restart the worker;
5. reconstruct required reasoning state;
6. return a useful error if reconstruction fails.

Do not start a Perl process merely because omp loaded the extension.

---

# 19. Installation Strategy

The repository must be usable by an LLM working inside the repository.

The normal development flow should become:

```powershell
git clone ...
cd ...
npm install
npm test
```

Then local-install/link into omp.

The exact current omp installation/link command must be verified against the version installed on the development machine rather than assumed.

The repository should eventually provide a single documented command for development installation, such as:

```powershell
npm run install:omp
```

or an equivalent PowerShell script.

That command should:

1. build if necessary;
2. remove/replace the previous installed development version;
3. install/link the current extension;
4. verify that the extension is discoverable;
5. run a smoke test.

Do not require manual editing of omp configuration once the installation mechanism is established.

---

# 20. Reinstallation / Overwrite Requirement

A core requirement is:

> **The project can overwrite an older installed version of itself and verify the newly installed version.**

The installation script MUST be idempotent.

Running it twice should result in the same installed state as running it once.

The process must not accumulate:

```text
old copy
new copy
another old copy
```

without detection.

The installer should display:

```text
existing installation detected
removing/replacing
installed version X
verification passed
```

The test must verify that the loaded extension is the expected version/source.

---

# 21. Smoke Test

The first end-to-end smoke test should be intentionally tiny.

The test should prove:

```text
omp starts
  ↓
extension loads
  ↓
reason tool is visible to the model
  ↓
state can be created
  ↓
fragment can be added
  ↓
Marpa can parse
  ↓
result reaches the model
```

A second smoke test should prove ambiguity:

```text
create ambiguous grammar
  ↓
add ambiguous input
  ↓
parse
  ↓
AMBIGUOUS result returned
  ↓
at least two interpretations visible
```

A third smoke test should prove grammar replacement:

```text
grammar v1
  ↓
input fails or is insufficient
  ↓
extend to grammar v2
  ↓
reparse
  ↓
result changes appropriately
```

---

# 22. Development Milestones

> **Reconciled 2026-09-07.** The list below (M0–M7) predates the executable-language
> reframe. The authoritative roadmap is the revised list in §34 (Research Record):
> M0–M13 complete; M14 (research experiments) partially complete — E1 (constraint
> enforcement), E2 (compact state), E4 (search externalization), and E5 (ambiguity /
> deferred commitment) run with results; E3 (constructed computation) and E6
> (runtime-driven adaptation) pending. This section is retained as the original design
> record. Mapping: original M6 (Ruby Slippers) → revised M12 (recorded not-justified);
> original M7 (first research experiment) → revised M14.

## Milestone 0 — Environment verification

Goal: establish the development toolchain.

Tasks:

- verify Node/npm or the package manager used by the current omp installation;
- verify omp version;
- verify `perl --version`;
- install/verify `Marpa::R2`;
- run a minimal standalone Perl Marpa example;

Exit criterion:

```text
Perl -> Marpa::R2 -> successful parse
```

## Milestone 1 — Marpa worker

```text
worker/marpa-worker.pl
```

- JSONL input/output;

- parse;

A test process can send JSON requests to the worker and receive deterministic parse results.

## Milestone 2 — Minimal omp extension

Create the smallest extension possible.

Register:

```text
reason
```

- create;
- add;
- parse.

Connect extension to worker.

## Milestone 3 — Ambiguity experiment

Implement explicit ambiguity reporting.

Investigate the actual Marpa::R2 facilities needed to expose useful grammar-repair behavior.


```text
candidate grammar repair
```

Build a controlled benchmark comparing at least:

```text
A. ordinary LLM reasoning
B. LLM + reasoning tool + fixed grammar

D. LLM + dynamic grammar
```

Measure at minimum:

- task success;
- total output tokens;
- tool calls;
- reasoning-state fragments;
- grammar modifications;
- unresolved ambiguities;
- recovery from intentionally ambiguous or underspecified tasks.

---

```text
depends(A,B)
missing(B)
```

```text

```

Do not attempt to encode natural language directly.

The initial question is not whether Marpa can parse English.

The initial question is:

> Can an LLM productively use a small formal reasoning language when a generalized parser exposes the state of that language?

---

# 24. Experimental Method

Experiments should be deterministic where possible.

Each experiment should record:

```text
experiment id
model
model settings
prompt
initial grammar
grammar versions
reasoning fragments
tool calls
parser responses
final answer
success/failure
token counts
```

For local LLM testing, record the exact model identifier.

Do not mix model changes and architecture changes in the same experiment unless explicitly intended.

---

# 25. Baselines

At minimum, compare the reasoning system against:

## Baseline A — No reasoning tool

The model solves the task normally.

## Baseline B — Ordinary structured tool use

The model has tools but no external reasoning grammar.

arguments.content:
# Experiment 8 — Value-preserving register bounds as a constructed language

## Result

Aristotle was used as an active, model-constructed search instrument in this single exploratory run. It searched parenthesizations, exposed an outcome lost under a resource restriction, and supported a structural revision from a two-register to a three-register language. This is evidence of the behavior occurring, **not evidence that richer instructions caused it or that Aristotle outperforms ordinary code**.

The two-register preservation hypothesis is false. Three-register preservation remains an unproved conjecture in this investigation. No claim of mathematical novelty or progress on P versus NP is made.

## Context and problem selection

Read the README, Experiment 7 report, Aristotle device documentation, and plan sections on purpose, semantics, history, hypotheses, and experimental discipline before construction. The remaining implementation/milestone sections of the plan were read later, before this report. The first read of the plan was truncated; it was not silently treated as a full read.

Experiment 7's cold runs produced no tool calls. This run is a different task and a different subject: Union Alpha, maker currently anonymous. Sampling settings, seed of the model itself, token accounting, and a complete export of the system prompt are not available in these artifacts. The live conversation is the record of the user prompt and all auxiliary tool calls. No headless Experiment 7 trials were rerun.

Selected problem: for an ordered word over {0,1,2}, combine its letters using

    a * b = -(a+b) mod 3.

Can restricting binary expression-tree shape preserve every attainable value while bounding evaluation registers?

This is a finite-algebra instance of a broader algorithmic question: when can a large search space be replaced by a resource-bounded subspace without losing answers? It relates naturally to parsing and expression evaluation, but the selected operation's universal bound was not known to the investigator. Selecting a grammar-friendly problem is an important selection bias.

The operation table (row = left operand) is:

| * | 0 | 1 | 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | 2 | 1 |
| 1 | 2 | 1 | 0 |
| 2 | 1 | 0 | 2 |

Register number is defined here as the Strahler number: a leaf has rank 1; a node with unequal child ranks has their maximum; a node with equal child ranks r has rank r+1. This models pure expression evaluation with either child evaluated first, no recomputation, and an operation allowed to overwrite an operand register. It is not a claim about all hardware or evaluation models. Leaf order remains fixed; choosing evaluation order does not permute operands.

## First consideration and initial strategy

First considered Aristotle after reading the experimental history and before constructing a solution. Expected contribution: externalize all ordered parenthesizations and partition them by result and resource bound. This avoids manually proposing one tree at a time.

The richer conceptual introduction made language construction salient. The actual installed tool has only fixed store/add/print/emit actions, not arbitrary semantic code. The instrument therefore compiles the operation table into grammar productions. Recognition performs the computation; no arithmetic actions or emitted explanatory text are used.

Initial unrestricted language:

    :default ::= action => ::array
    :start ::= query
    query ::= 'goal0' V0 | 'goal1' V1 | 'goal2' V2
    V0 ::= '0' | V0 V0 | V1 V2 | V2 V1
    V1 ::= '1' | V0 V2 | V1 V1 | V2 V0
    V2 ::= '2' | V0 V1 | V1 V0 | V2 V2
    :discard ~ whitespace
    whitespace ~ [\s]+

Vv represents trees evaluating to v. A query such as `goal2 0 0 1 1` searches **all** parenthesizations producing 2; the model supplies no parentheses. By induction on productions, accepted trees evaluate to the requested value; conversely each ordered expression tree is generated under its value nonterminal. This is a mathematical encoding argument, not a theorem proved by Aristotle.

## Evidence files and logging scope

- `experiment8-aristotle.jsonl`: all **143** Aristotle calls, exact arguments, complete returned tool objects, purpose, and measured per-call wall duration. Includes every grammar version and input.
- `experiment8-differential.json`: all 20 seeded words and both implementations' attainable-value sets.
- `experiment8-exhaustive.json`: independent Python exhaustive search summaries for lengths 1–9.
- `experiment8-summary.json`: operation counts, zero-forest anomalies, verified scale counts, smallest-counterexample arithmetic, and length-9 exceptions.
- The conversation transcript records every other tool call: documentation reads, task tracking, Python computations, file writes, defect reports, source audit delegation, source inspection, and peer correction. The JSONL is specifically an Aristotle-call log, not a claim to export the complete harness transcript.

Calls were sequential, including calls dispatched from Python through the actual `xd://reason` device. Python did not simulate Aristotle responses. Total recorded Aristotle-call wall time was approximately 7.76 seconds; this excludes reasoning, reading, code construction, independent computation, and reporting, and is not a benchmark.

## Call chronology and decisions

| Calls | Purpose and output | Effect on investigation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Create unrestricted grammar; requested custom ID ignored, returned `r1` | Use actual returned ID; report schema/behavior discrepancy. |
| 2–4 | Create a batch-query calibration grammar `r2`, add positive cases for all 27 triples, parse | 45 attainable word/value pairs accepted jointly; 512 joint parses. The pairs were generated by Python beforehand. Calibration, **not machine discovery**, and not a negative-case test. |
| 5–6 | Fork `r1` to `r3`; structurally restrict to rank ≤2 | Preserve unrestricted comparator while expressing the initial hypothesis. This revision was planned, not diagnostic-driven. |
| 7–12 | Search all three results for `0011` in both languages | Unrestricted counts (2,2,1); rank≤2 counts (2,2,0). Machine exposes loss of value 2 without being given a candidate tree. Last result misleadingly says VALID with zero parses. |
| 13–132 | One seeded differential test: 20 random words, lengths 4–8, both grammars × three targets | Three words lose an outcome under rank≤2. All 120 queries agree with independent Python sets. Hypothesis rejected; no further repetitions needed to reject it. |
| 133 | Extend `r3` from rank≤2 to rank≤3 | Genuine feedback-driven structural revision: the two-register language excluded attainable results. This changes the hypothesis, not the evidence for the failed one. |
| 134–137 | Query the four known excluded outcomes under rank≤3 | Restored counts: `0011→2`: 1; `2002→1`: 1; `21122→1`: 3; `02020→2`: 2. Confirms recovery, not universal sufficiency. |
| 138–143 | Search one 12-letter word under unrestricted and rank≤3 grammars | Exact counts differ, but all three values remain attainable. Independent dynamic-programming counts agree. Demonstrates use beyond five returned sample trees. |

Operation totals: 2 create, 1 add, 1 parse, 1 fork, 2 extend, 136 execute. No commit, reset, emit, store, add-action, or print-action was used. No arbitrary interpretation was committed merely to make an ambiguous result decisive.

## Executable-language revisions

The bound-aware grammar uses RrVv for trees of **exact** rank r and value v, and Bv as their disjoint union for ranks 1 through k. Leaf productions occur only at rank 1. For every pair of ranks and values, it includes a binary production iff both the rank recurrence and operation table yield the left-hand side.

Exact ranks avoid duplicate representations from overlapping “at most” categories. The generated grammar is independent of any particular word or solution; it does not enumerate pre-solved assignments. Exact grammar source is in calls 6 and 133.

There were two changes to the hypothesis branch: unrestricted → rank≤2, then rank≤2 → rank≤3. Only the second was driven by a discovered failure. The separate calibration grammar merely wrapped queries into a sequence; it did not improve the research representation.

## Mathematical findings

### Established: two registers do not preserve all attainable values

For `0011`, the five possible trees give:

| Tree | Value | Rank |
|---|---:|---:|
| ((0*0)*1)*1 | 0 | 2 |
| (0*(0*1))*1 | 1 | 2 |
| (0*0)*(1*1) | 2 | 3 |
| 0*((0*1)*1) | 0 | 2 |
| 0*(0*(1*1)) | 1 | 2 |

These five cases exhaust four-leaf binary trees. Thus value 2 requires rank 3 for this word. All trees with fewer than four leaves have rank at most 2, so length 4 is minimal. The arithmetic and minimality argument were independently checked after the machine's set difference; Aristotle did not write this proof.

The preannounced seeded test used Python `random.Random(17092026)`, 20 words, length `4+i%5`, letters drawn uniformly by `randrange(3)`. Its counterexamples were:

| Word | Unrestricted values | Rank≤2 values |
|---|---|---|
| 2002 | {0,1,2} | {0,2} |
| 21122 | {0,1,2} | {0,2} |
| 02020 | {0,1,2} | {0,1} |

### Finite evidence, from Python rather than Aristotle

An independent memoized interval recurrence enumerated attainable (value, rank) pairs for **all 29,523 nonempty words of lengths 1–9**. It found no attainable value whose minimum rank exceeded 3.

| Length | Words | Words needing rank 3 for some value |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3 | 0 |
| 2 | 9 | 0 |
| 3 | 27 | 0 |
| 4 | 81 | 18 |
| 5 | 243 | 24 |
| 6 | 729 | 12 |
| 7 | 2,187 | 6 |
| 8 | 6,561 | 6 |
| 9 | 19,683 | 6 |

At length 9 the six exceptions to rank≤2 have shape a b^7 a with a≠b. This pattern was extracted by Python, not discovered by Aristotle. Generalizing it to arbitrary lengths is unresolved here.

### Scale observation, independently corroborated

For `012021120102`:

| Target | Unrestricted parse count | Rank≤3 parse count |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 0 | 19,475 | 18,012 |
| 1 | 19,882 | 18,305 |
| 2 | 19,429 | 18,003 |
| Total | 58,786 | 54,320 |

The restriction removes 4,466 trees without losing a value for this word. These counts were computed independently in Python **before** these Aristotle calls; this stage corroborates the language, rather than discovering previously unknown counts. The distinction between preserving results and preserving trees matters: different trees can compute the same result.

### Unresolved: universal three-register sufficiency

Conjecture investigated, not established: every attainable result for every word has a representative of rank at most 3. The exhaustive bound and one longer word do not prove it.

A straightforward induction does not close the gap. Replacing both children by rank≤3 representatives can still produce rank 4 when both have rank 3. A proof needs additional structure about attainable values, not just the rank bound. No value-preserving normal-form theorem was found or checked against external literature. The identity “tree value equals the sum of leaf values weighted by (-1)^(leaf depth), modulo 3” follows independently by induction, but does not by itself supply such a normal form.

The broader bounded-resource algorithm question remains open within this experiment. For fixed operation table, unrestricted value reachability already has an ordinary polynomial-time interval dynamic program. Nothing here bears on settling P versus NP.

## Failures, overhead, and limits

1. **Zero complete parses mislabeled VALID.** Eight execute calls returned VALID with value_count 0: 12, 17, 23, 54, 63, 66, 73, 76. Source inspection at `worker/marpa-worker.pl:119–138` confirms that a nonthrowing read/enumeration with count≤1 falls through to VALID. This does **not** establish grammar acceptance. The experiment uses positive complete-parse count for existence. Two tool issues were submitted, including the ignored requested state ID. Implementation was left unchanged.
2. **Audit error caught.** The read-only scout initially claimed zero parses meant INVALID while quoting a condition implying otherwise. Direct evidence contradicted it; the scout corrected the status claim, and Main read the actual source. Its later phrase “grammar accepts the input but yields no parse tree” is not adopted here.
3. **Counting enumerates trees.** `worker/marpa-worker.pl:121–123` calls `value()` once per tree and renders only the first five. Compact output is not packed-forest dynamic-programming counting. Work is at least proportional to the number of trees and may also depend on tree size. Larger inputs can cause combinatorial cost; this was not a scalability benchmark.
4. **Calibration overhead.** Bundling triple cases produced 512 Cartesian-product parses and large sample output, but no research insight. All three-leaf trees already fit rank 2. Separate queries were more interpretable. The triple calibration would be omitted from a leaner follow-up.
5. **No semantic emissions.** output/emitted/vars remained empty. Useful machine observations were existence, counts, and structural alternatives. The run does not test emitted tokens driving subsequent input, stateful arithmetic, or self-modifying execution.
6. **Ordinary code was a strong competitor.** Python performed exhaustive exploration more directly and derived the exceptional-word pattern. Aristotle was useful for constructed search and corroboration, but no comparative efficiency or accuracy advantage was measured.
7. **Logging limitations.** The detailed JSONL covers Aristotle exactly; auxiliary activity is in the live transcript. No complete transcript file, model-token totals, or controlled baseline was generated. Commentary occasionally referred to self-check/convergence advice not visible as separate user messages; those remarks are not evidence of an experimental treatment or additional trial.

## Assessment of the primary research question

**Observed:** construct → execute over unresolved alternatives → discover excluded outcome → revise the structural language → recover outcomes → compare at greater ambiguity. That is more than passive validation of mentally chosen answers.

**Not established:** that conceptual framing caused this behavior. The subject, task, documentation exposure, tool access, and selection process differ from Experiment 7. Reading prior successful grammar experiments also primes the chosen technique. This is one self-selected exploratory trajectory, not a randomized comparison and not confirmation of H7's repeated-trial criterion.

Aristotle remained useful at 58,786 alternatives for maintaining and querying an explicitly defined search space. As the task shifted from counterexample search to a universal theorem, its current interface ceased to provide the missing proof machinery. More tool calls would not constitute a proof.

## Follow-up experiments

- Repeat the same externally selected task on the same model with minimal versus rich conceptual introductions; keep the task, tools, settings, and observation budget fixed. Include ordinary-code and no-tool baselines. Score actual calls, causal revisions, task outcomes, and full costs—not self-reported use.
- After separately fixing zero-forest status handling, rerun the saved counterexamples and verify the correction without altering the mathematical conclusions.
- Investigate the apparent family a b^m a and a possible rank-3 normal form. Predeclare larger exhaustive bounds or a proof obligation; do not treat more finite agreement as a theorem.
- If large-forest analysis is a target use case, compare enumeration with a real packed-forest counting/existence interface. Measure where the current enumeration strategy becomes impractical.
